links.outcome: Correlation of WER and other ASR metrics with clinician-assigned clinical risk labels
links.effect: WER and a comprehensive suite of existing metrics correlated poorly with clinician-assigned risk labels (No, Minimal, Significant Impact); the optimized LLM judge reached 90% accuracy and Cohen's kappa 0.816.
links.quote: Our analysis reveals that WER and a comprehensive suite of existing metrics correlate poorly with the clinician-assigned risk labels (No, Minimal, or Significant Impact).

unlisted_practices: Using a GEPA/DSPy-optimized LLM-as-a-Judge to score the clinical impact of ASR transcription errors instead of relying on WER

screen.reason: The paper investigates the clinical safety risks of ASR transcription errors in clinical dialogue and evaluates an LLM-as-a-judge framework as an automated safety evaluation safeguard/practice to catch clinically significant errors.

primary.practice: automated safety evaluation of transcription errors
